title: Prefixes: creating new meanings
subtitle: in-, mis-, out-, re-, over-, under-, up-
summary: Build and decode advanced vocabulary from its prefixes - in-, mis-, out-, re-, eco- and e-, the three meanings each of over- and under-, and the Latin prefixes con-, pro- and e-.

lesson.heading: Common prefixes
rows: misbehave, misuse (use in the wrong way or for the wrong purpose)
outnumber (be larger in number than), outweigh (be greater or more important than)
reconsider (think again about a decision), redevelop, rethink
e-commerce (buying and selling goods online), e-reader, e-cigarettes
eco-friendly cleaning products, an eco-city, an eco-warrior
lesson.note: An eco-city uses energy efficiently and produces very little pollution; an eco-warrior is an informal name for someone who campaigns to protect the environment.

lesson.heading: The prefix over-: three meanings
rows: That film was overrated in my view.
people said it was better than it really was
It was a bad restaurant, with an overpriced menu.
Several of our neighbour's large trees overhang our garden.
their branches go over our garden
Our garden is overshadowed by the block of flats next door.
the flats cast a shadow over it; metaphorically, she felt overshadowed by her sister
He overstepped the mark when he said that.
crossed a barrier into unacceptable behaviour
crossing from one day to the next

lesson.heading: The prefix under-: three meanings
rows: Don't underestimate the time it will take.
think it will be less than it really is
on the ground, beneath your feet
The underlying question is a very difficult one.
I wish you would not undermine everything I do.
He did it in a very underhand way.

lesson.heading: The prefix up-
lesson.text: **up-** can suggest a change of some kind, often a positive one.

examples.text: The airline **upgraded** me to business class.
examples.note: = changed my ticket to a better class

examples.text: There has been an **upturn** in the economy.

lesson.heading: Less frequent prefixes
rows: mixing things together, often in verbs of communication
converse (chat; formal), commiserate (sympathise with someone's unhappiness), condolences, congeal (change from liquid to solid), contaminate (make poisonous or less pure)
pushing something forward or increasing it
promote (encourage people to buy or use something), proliferate (suddenly increase a lot in number), procrastinate (keep delaying something), procreate (produce young; formal)
eject (throw out with force; formal), emit (send out a beam, noise, smell or gas; formal)
lesson.note: They were ejected from the restaurant for bad behaviour. The machine emitted a loud noise and then stopped working.

lesson.text: With over- and under-, ask yourself whether the word is about too much/too little, about position, or about behaviour - the same prefix does all three jobs.

exercises.prompt: They are planning to ___ the area around the old bus station.
exercises.explanation: The prefix re- means do again.

exercises.prompt: It is ___ to use informal language in a formal essay.
exercises.explanation: in- (and its variations im-, il-, ir-) makes a word negative.

exercises.prompt: The yes votes ___ the no votes by two to one.
exercises.explanation: To outnumber a group is to be larger in number than it.

exercises.prompt: Ivan's English is excellent but he still tends to ___ idioms occasionally.
exercises.explanation: mis- means wrongly or badly: to misuse something is to use it in the wrong way.

exercises.prompt: We all hope you will ___ your decision to turn down our offer of a job.
exercises.explanation: To reconsider is to think again about a decision or opinion.

exercises.prompt: An ___ to drive is a serious problem for anyone in this line of business.
exercises.explanation: The negative prefix in- turns ability into inability.

exercises.prompt: Paula lost marks in her science test because of the ___ of her measurements.
More and more businesses use the internet to sell their products, so ___ is becoming more important to the economy.
exercises.explanation: The prefix e- means electronic; e-commerce is buying and selling goods online.

exercises.prompt: More farmers are now choosing to use ___ fertilisers that don't harm the environment or wildlife.
exercises.explanation: eco- means good for the environment.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite: The hotel gave me a luxury room instead of the ordinary one I'd booked. The hotel ___ me to a luxury room.
exercises.explanation: up- often suggests a positive change: to upgrade someone is to move them to a better class.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite: For me, the advantages of air travel are more significant than the disadvantages. The advantages ___ the disadvantages.
exercises.explanation: To outweigh something is to be greater or more important than it.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite: It's slippery walking just here. It's slippery ___ just here.
exercises.explanation: Underfoot means on the ground, beneath your feet.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite: I felt that what she said was critical of my position and weakened it. I felt that what she said ___ my position.
exercises.explanation: To undermine something is to attack or weaken it - a negative use of under-.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'It would be a mistake to think Frances is less intelligent than she really is'?
options: It would be a mistake to underestimate Frances's intelligence.
It would be a mistake to overrate Frances's intelligence.
It would be a mistake to undermine Frances's intelligence.
It would be a mistake to outweigh Frances's intelligence.
exercises.explanation: To underestimate something is to think it is less than it really is.

exercises.prompt: 'It was a bad restaurant, with an overpriced menu.' Which meaning of over- is this?
exercises.explanation: Overpriced means the prices were too high - the 'excess' meaning of over-.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with the definition it matches.

pairs.right: keep delaying something that must be done
make something poisonous or less pure
suddenly increase a lot in number
change from a liquid or soft state to a solid one
send out a beam, noise, smell or gas

exercises.prompt: Which pair gives the formal words for 'to throw out with force' and 'to chat'?
exercises.explanation: Eject means to throw out with force; converse is the formal word for chat.

exercises.statement: If someone does something in an underhand way, they do it openly and honestly.
exercises.explanation: The opposite - underhand means secretly and possibly dishonestly.

exercises.prompt: In each of these words, which meaning does the prefix carry?
